To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bile acids and the gut microbiota are critical regulators of diabetes, obesity, non-alcoholic fatty disease, cardiovascular disease, and aging, and that targeting bile acid signaling and gut microbiome may be a promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of these diseases.
Bile acids are metabolic hormones and nutrients that are synthesized and transformed in the gut by bacteria.

1) bile acid signaling regulates glucose, lipid, and energy metabolism; 2) bile acid signaling protects against obesity and diabetes; 3) gut dysbiosis and bile acid dysmetabolism contribute to the development of diabetes and obesity; 4) bile acid and microbiome-targeted therapies have therapeutic potential for diabetes and obesity; and 5) bile acid signaling and gut microbiome are therapeutic targets for diabetes and obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of bile acids in the pathogenesis of diabetes and obesity, and how bile acid signaling and gut bacteria can be targeted for therapeutic benefit.
the role of the gut microbiome, bile acid metabolism and the gut-liver-brain axis in the pathophysiology of metabolic diseases.
the understanding of the role of bile acids and gut microbiome in diabetes and obesity, and the identification of new therapeutic targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gut microbiome, bile acids, and their receptors are key players in the pathophysiology of diabetes and its complications and may serve as therapeutic targets.
bile acids are important for maintaining glucose homeostasis.

1) bile acids regulate lipid, glucose and energy homeostases by activating FXR and TGR5; 2) bile acids control gut bacteria composition; 3) gut bacteria control bile acid composition and bile acid pool size; and 4) dysregulation of bile acids and dysbiosis cause diabetes, obesity, NAFLD and CVD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

bile acid signaling and gut microbiota are key players in diabetes and obesity and that therapeutic targeting of bile acid signaling or gut microbiome may have potential to treat diabetes and obesity.
bile acid signaling in diabetes, obesity, non-alcoholic fatty acid disease, and gut microbiome is a promising target for therapeutic intervention.

bile acid signaling is a promising target for treating diabetes and obesity, but more studies are needed to fully understand the role of the gut microbiome in bile acid signaling and metabolic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bile acid signaling is an emerging therapeutic target for treating diabetes, metabolic disorders, and liver diseases.
the bile acid-gut microbiome axis is a promising target for diabetes treatment.
bile acids and the gut microbiota are important regulators of diabetes and obesity.
